nodes.summary: The admixture-graph drift model, stated at the level of second moments.
nodes.title: Admixture-graph drift model

nodes.summary: `f2` is symmetric.
nodes.title: Symmetry of the f2 statistic

nodes.summary: `f2` is the special case `f4 A B A B`.
nodes.title: f2 as a special case of f4

nodes.summary: With binary loadings `f2 X Y` is the total drift length of the edges in exactly one of the weight-`1` edge sets of `X` and `Y`. On a tree, where these sets are the root-to-`X` and root-to-`Y` paths, this is the additive tree distance between `X` and `Y`.
nodes.title: f2 as a symmetric-difference drift length under binary loadings

nodes.summary: `f2` in the drift model: `f2 X Y = ∑ e, (w X e - w Y e) ^ 2 * len e`.
nodes.title: f2 in the drift model

nodes.summary: `f2` is nonnegative.
nodes.title: Nonnegativity of the f2 statistic
f2 of a population with itself is zero

nodes.summary: The statistic `f2 X Y = 𝔼[(p X - p Y) ^ 2]`, the expected squared allele-frequency difference between populations `X` and `Y`.
nodes.title: f2 statistic

nodes.summary: Admixture followed by drift: if `C` is an `α : 1 - α` mixture of `A` and `B` that then drifts along a private edge `c` (not traversed by `A` or `B`), then `f3 C A B = len c - α (1 - α) f2 A B`; post-admixture drift can mask the admixture signal.
nodes.title: f3 of an admixture followed by drift

nodes.summary: If `C` is a mixture of `A` and `B` in proportions `α : 1 - α` (with no subsequent drift), then `f3 C A B = -α (1 - α) f2 A B`.
nodes.title: f3 of a pure admixture

nodes.summary: `f3` in terms of `f2`: `f3 C A B = (f2 C A + f2 C B - f2 A B) / 2`.
nodes.title: f3 in terms of f2

nodes.summary: `f3` is the special case `f4 C A C B`.
nodes.title: f3 as a special case of f4

nodes.summary: `f3` in the drift model: `f3 C A B = ∑ e, (w C e - w A e) * (w C e - w B e) * len e`.
nodes.title: f3 in the drift model

nodes.summary: Three-population test, converse direction: a nondegenerate pure admixture (`0 < α < 1`, `f2 A B > 0`) yields a negative `f3 C A B`.
nodes.title: Nondegenerate pure admixture gives negative f3

nodes.summary: With binary loadings `f3` is nonnegative; on a tree it is the drift length of the path from `C` to the `A–B` path.
nodes.title: f3 is nonnegative under binary loadings

nodes.summary: The statistic `f3 C A B = 𝔼[(p C - p A) * (p C - p B)]` of a target population `C` against two source populations `A` and `B`.
nodes.title: f3 statistic

nodes.summary: If `X` is an `α : 1 - α` mixture of `Y` and `C`, then `f4 A O X C = α * f4 A O Y C` (bilinearity of `f4`, together with `f4 A O C C = 0`).
nodes.title: f4 of an admixed population scales with the mixture proportion

nodes.summary: `f4` is symmetric under exchanging the two pairs.
nodes.title: f4 is symmetric under exchanging the two pairs

nodes.summary: `f4` in terms of `f2`: `f4 A B C D = (f2 A D + f2 B C - f2 A C - f2 B D) / 2`.
nodes.title: f4 in terms of f2

nodes.summary: `f4 A B C D = 0` when no edge contributes to both the `A–B` and the `C–D` path. On a tree with split `AB | CD` the paths `A–B` and `C–D` share no edge, so this hypothesis holds.
nodes.title: f4 vanishes for edge-disjoint paths

nodes.summary: `f4` in the drift model: the root cancels, and `f4 A B C D` is the drift length shared by the paths `A–B` and `C–D`, weighted by `(w A e - w B e) * (w C e - w D e)`.
nodes.title: f4 in the drift model

nodes.summary: f4-ratio estimation of the admixture proportion. f4-ratio estimation (Patterson et al. 2012). Let `X` be an `α : 1 - α` mixture of a source lineage `Y` and of `C`, where `Y` is unsampled but sister to the sampled population `B` relative to the `A–O` path, so that `f4 A O Y C = f4 A O B C`. If this value is nonzero, the ratio `f4 A O X C / f4 A O B C` of two estimable statistics recovers the admixture proportion `α`.
nodes.title: f4-ratio estimation of the admixture proportion

nodes.summary: `f4` changes sign when the first pair is swapped.
nodes.title: f4 changes sign when the first pair is swapped

nodes.summary: `f4` changes sign when the second pair is swapped.
nodes.title: f4 changes sign when the second pair is swapped

nodes.summary: The statistic `f4 A B C D = 𝔼[(p A - p B) * (p C - p D)]`.
nodes.title: f4 statistic

nodes.summary: The allele frequency of population `X`: the root frequency plus the weighted sum of the drift increments of the edges traversed by lineages from `X`.
nodes.title: Allele frequency of a population in the drift model

nodes.summary: `F_ST = (H_T - H_S) / H_T` is nonnegative for nonnegative weights summing to `1`. The ratio is defined only when `H_T > 0` (at a fixed allele `H_T = H_S = 0`), so that is assumed.
nodes.title: Nonnegativity of the fixation index $F_{ST}$

nodes.summary: The model has binary loadings if every lineage weight is `0` or `1`.
nodes.title: Binary loadings of a drift model

nodes.summary: The Wahlund effect: with nonnegative weights summing to `1`, subdivision lowers heterozygosity, `H_S ≤ H_T`.
nodes.title: Wahlund effect

nodes.summary: Mean within-subpopulation (Hardy–Weinberg) heterozygosity `H_S = ∑ i, c i * 2 q i (1 - q i)`.
nodes.title: Mean within-subpopulation heterozygosity

nodes.summary: Total heterozygosity `H_T = 2 q̄ (1 - q̄)` expected under random mating of the pooled population.
nodes.title: Total heterozygosity of the pooled population

nodes.summary: A difference of square-integrable frequencies has integrable square.
nodes.title: Square of a difference of square-integrable frequencies is integrable

nodes.summary: Bilinearity of the second moment of increments: `𝔼[(∑ e, a e * incr e) * (∑ f, b f * incr f)] = ∑ e, a e * b e * len e`.
nodes.title: Bilinearity of the second moment of drift increments

nodes.summary: Drift lengths are nonnegative.
nodes.title: Drift lengths are nonnegative

nodes.summary: The edges of weight `1` for population `X`; on a tree, the root-to-`X` lineage.
nodes.title: Lineage of a population in the drift model

nodes.summary: Mean allele frequency `q̄ = ∑ i, c i * q i` of a population made of subpopulations with weights `c i` and allele frequencies `q i`.
nodes.title: Mean allele frequency of a subdivided population

nodes.summary: Population frequencies are square integrable.
nodes.title: Population frequencies are square integrable

nodes.summary: A weighted sum of increments is square integrable.
nodes.title: Weighted sum of drift increments is square integrable

nodes.summary: Three-population test: a negative `f3 C A B` is incompatible with binary loadings, hence with every tree model.
nodes.title: Three-population test: negative f3 rules out a tree

nodes.summary: Wahlund identity: for weights summing to `1`, `H_T - H_S = 2 ∑ i, c i * (q i - q̄) ^ 2`, twice the weighted variance of subpopulation frequencies.
nodes.title: Wahlund identity

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
